name: Password strength meter
summary: A meter under a new-password field that scores what is typed and gives plain-language advice.
description: Point data-v-strength on the password input at a <meter>. The element right after the meter shows your rules while the field is empty and short advice once typing starts. It is a guide, not a rule: enforce the real minimum with minlength.

states.description: Set by the JS from 0 (too short) to 4 (strong). Give the meter min="0" max="4" low="2" high="3" optimum="4" so the colours follow.
Set by the JS to the level in words (Weak, Fair, Good, Strong), or Empty.

hooks.name: data-v-strength
hooks.value: CSS selector of the meter, e.g. #pw-meter
hooks.description: Scores the password on each input and updates the meter and the hint after it.

a11y: The meter needs a name (aria-label="Password strength"); its level is read as words through aria-valuetext.
The level is announced politely only when it changes, not on every key.
Show the rules before typing starts, in the hint after the meter, so nothing is hidden until it fails.
Link the hint to the input with aria-describedby so the advice is read with the field.

examples.title: New password
examples.description: Try "password1", then a few unrelated words.
examples.html: At least 8 characters, 12 or more is better. A few unrelated words work well.
